title: まま: the unchanged condition
summary: まま is a noun meaning "an unchanged condition". Every use of it, from そのまま to わがまま, comes from that one idea.

blocks.text: Grammar lists give まま a pile of meanings ("as it is", "as one wishes", "a state") and even call it a particle. Use the word-type test from lesson 41 instead. まま does not end in an う-row kana and does not end in い, so it is a **noun**. Which noun? An **unchanged condition**. Whenever you see まま, read "unchanged condition".

Because まま is a noun, anything that describes it comes before it: another noun with **の**, an い-adjective, or a whole verb phrase. The word carries an extra hint: the condition could have changed, but it has not.

blocks.jp: 自然のままの森を歩いた。
blocks.en: (I) walked through a forest in its natural, untouched state.

blocks.jp: パジャマのまま朝ごはんを食べた。
blocks.en: (I) ate breakfast still in my pajamas.

blocks.jp: いつまでも若いままでいたい。
窓を開けたまま寝てしまった。
blocks.en: (I) fell asleep with the window left open.

blocks.text: まま often takes the copula で ("being the unchanged condition"). Like a time expression it may drop that で, which is why そのままで食べる and そのまま食べる are both fine. The meaning is "while it stays in its unchanged condition".

In 思いのまま and 心のまま, the "unchanged condition" is a match with your own thoughts or heart. The world outside stays just as the inside wants it. 思いのままに動けない means "(I) cannot move as I wish". From the same idea comes **わがまま**: わが is "my", so it is "my own unchanged condition", a person who wants the world to follow their will. That is selfishness.

items: まま is a **noun**: an **unchanged condition**.
The describing part goes before it: **Nのまま**, **い-adjective + まま**, **verb (た / ない) + まま**.
The で after it can drop: そのまま食べる.
**思いのまま** = as one wishes; **わがまま** = my own way, selfish.

questions.instruction: What kind of word is まま?
questions.note: It has no verb or adjective ending, so it is a noun.

questions.instruction: Pick the meaning of まま
questions.note: Every use of まま comes back to this.

questions.prompt: 靴を履いた＿＿部屋に入った。 ((I) went into the room with shoes still on.)
questions.note: 履いた + まま: the shoes stayed on, an unchanged condition.

questions.prompt: テレビをつけたまま寝た。
options: (I) fell asleep with the TV left on
(I) turned on the TV after sleeping
questions.note: つけた + まま: the TV stayed on.

questions.instruction: Tap the noun that means "unchanged condition"
questions.note: パジャマの describes it; 食べた is the engine.

questions.instruction: Which phrase means "in its natural, untouched state"?
questions.note: A noun describes まま with の.

questions.prompt: In そのまま食べる, the で may be dropped because まま behaves like a time expression.
questions.note: そのままで食べる and そのまま食べる are both used.

questions.instruction: What is the literal sense of わがまま?
questions.note: わが is "my"; wanting the world to follow your will reads as selfish.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "(I) want to stay as I am"?
questions.note: このまま + で + いたい: be in this unchanged condition.

questions.prompt: (I) ate breakfast still in my pajamas.
questions.note: パジャマのまま describes the condition, then the object and the verb.

questions.instruction: What does 思いのまま suggest?
options: The outside matches what is inside one's heart
questions.note: The world stays in the same condition as one's own thoughts.

questions.instruction: Which part tells you the condition could have changed but did not?
questions.note: That hint is part of what まま means.
